newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-India sub-continent demand, prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold-India sub-continent demand, prices seen mixed.

text.p: Gold demand in India, despite the availability of cheap imported gold, may ease this week while in neighbouring Pakistan prices are seen mixed, dealers said on Monday.
"World market sentiment is weak and the landing cost of imported gold in India is low," said dealer Bhayabhai Sanghvi.
But he said the next two weeks were deemed "inauspicious, according to the Hindu calendar to buy precious metals and I expect demand to remain low ..."
On the Bombay bullion market, gold prices were unchanged at 5,120 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday
"The low physical demand kept the market subdued in the early days of the week but later on it recovered on restricted inflows of smuggled gold," one trader said.
In Pakistan, dealers said gold prices were likely to remain mixed on low buying interest due to rupee fluctuations.
The fluctuation of the rupee would keep gold rates mixed, one Karachi dealer said.
Traders in Dubai said that Indian demand for gold was ahead of India's festival and wedding season.
Dubai is the main source of gold to India through official sales and smuggling by the large expatriate communities working in the oil-rich United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Local and re-export turnover in Dubai bullion and jewellery markets was steadily increasing ahead of the Hindu festival of Diwali in November and the second Indian marriage season running from November to April, traders said.
Both events are traditionally celebrated with purchases of gold -- bought from proceeds of the harvest -- to an extent that makes India the world's largest consumer of the metal.
"Indian goldsmiths and jewellers are buying ahead to meet the demand. The Indian harvest has been a good one this year," a Dubai trader said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion 1$=35.70 Indian rupees, 36.97 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices September 30 & 12, Karachi prices and Dubai September 29 & 22 respectively.
